items.title: Too close? Give them room.
items.caption:
Social skills rule: Respect the invisible force field.

Picture an invisible force field around every person.
When we stand too close, it can feel uncomfortable.
Step back and leave comfortable room.
If a friend moves away, give a little more space.

Find more practice in Social Skills Boot Camp by Arianna Andersen. Free parent activities at books.familygallerytv.com. Paperback on Amazon.

items.title: Not over the shoulder.
items.caption:
Not over the shoulder.

When a friend is sitting and looking at something, leaning over her shoulder crowds her. Say hi from a comfortable distance instead.

Social skills rule: Respect the invisible force field.

items.title: "Look at this!" Not in their face.
items.caption:
Social skills rule: Don't stick things in people's faces.

You finished a picture and you are so excited.
Holding it right in a friend's face can feel like too much.
Hold it at a comfortable distance.
Ask, "Want to see it?" Then wait.

Find more practice in Social Skills Boot Camp by Arianna Andersen. Free parent activities at books.familygallerytv.com. Paperback on Amazon.

items.title: A hug needs a yes.
items.caption:
Social skills rule: Ask before touching and respect the answer.

Hugs can be a sweet way to show you care.
Before you hug, ask: "Can I give you a hug?"
If the answer is yes, hug gently.
If the answer is no, smile or wave instead.

Find more practice in Social Skills Boot Camp by Arianna Andersen. Free parent activities at books.familygallerytv.com. Paperback on Amazon.

items.title: Not your favorite? Don't put it down.
items.caption:
Social skills rule: Don't yuck someone else's yum.

Riley got a new Minecraft lunchbox.
Noah said, "Minecraft is so dumb."
That yucked Riley's yum.
Try: "That's not for me, but I'm glad you like it."

Find more practice in Social Skills Boot Camp by Arianna Andersen. Free parent activities at books.familygallerytv.com. Paperback on Amazon.

items.title: A conversation needs turns.
items.caption:
Social skills rule: Return the turn.

A conversation is like playing catch.
One person talks, then passes the turn back.
Try a related answer plus a quick question.
"I like tag. What games do you like?"

Find more practice in Social Skills Boot Camp by Arianna Andersen. Free parent activities at books.familygallerytv.com. Paperback on Amazon.

Riley keeps going, and Olivia gets upset.
